messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] DB calls in RHIPE map/red script
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] DB calls in RHIPE map/red script
messages.body_plain:
Hi ,

thanks for the code, is there any extra documentation for accessing
the data from hbase to rhipe mapper other then this
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RhipeHbaseMozilla

Thanks and regards
Sandeep

On Sat, Sep 1, 2012 at 12:06 AM, Saptarshi Guha
<saptars...@gmail.com> wrote:
> sure, install some R package for mysql and load the library in the setup.
> Make the calls. Be sure your mysql can accept many simultaneous
> connections.
>
> This code actually writes to HBase from within a mapreduce job
>
>
> rhput("~/tmp/rbase.jar","/user/sguha/tmp")
> setup <- expression(map={
>  library(rJava)
>  library(rbase)
>  ra <- rb.init()
>  tb <- rb.table.connect(ra,"anewtable")
> })
> j <- rhwatch(rhmr(
>                   map=rhmap(after={
>                     tb$putMany(map.keys,
> values=lapply(map.values,function(r) list("y:a"=r,"y:b"=runif(1))))
>                   })
>                   ,reduce=0
>                   ,setup=setup
>                   ,N=1e6,mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=5000))
>
> Took  4 minutes on a 336 simultaneous map tasks -so not the best
> performance.
>
> On Thu, Aug 30, 2012 at 7:49 PM, sandy <sandeepb...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Hello Group,
>>
>> Can i make database calls to mysql or any database from RHIPE map/reduce
>> scripts. If so can you please share the code snippet.
>>
>>
>> Thanks in advance
>> Sandeep

messages.subject: Re: rhget and rhwrite errors in map function
messages.subject_clean: rhget and rhwrite errors in map function
messages.body_plain:
rhget is in the library package for Rhipe which is not loaded inside of the MapReduce environment unless you do so as you would for any R code.  See the setup argument of rhmr and use library(Rhipe).

Also, because rhget depends on a back-end rhipe java process I am not entirely sure that it is a solid scaling idea to do it that way in the Map.  You can do it.  It would probably work to a certain degree, but you may want to consider this closely.

>
>

>
>
>

>

> library(Rhipe)
>
> rhinit()

>
>
> # list of tar files – created and uploaded into HDFS before starting R
>
> # using shell script
>
> inputfilelist <- "/user/hduser/AZD2input/inputfilelist"
>
>
>
> map <- expression({
>
>   lapply(seq_along(map.values),function(r){
>
>
>
>        v <- map.values[[r]]
>
>
>
>        rhget(v, ".")
>
>        untar(v)
>
>
>
>         rhcollect(map.keys[[r]],c(map.values[[r]]))
>
>   })
>
> })
>
> ## Create a job object

>        inout=c('text','sequence'),
>
>        mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0),

>        jobname='test')

this wont work. Surprisingly, you cannot load (via library) RHIPE in in the mapreduce job.
you could do soemthing like

system(sprintf("hadoop dfs -get %s ./", filename))

or something like that ...
